dispositions.finding: src/cma/llm.py:87 (and :109): a hosted client created before the lock was turned on can still send a request
dispositions.evidence: test_existing_client_refused_once_the_lock_is_on[AnthropicLLM|OpenAILLM] failed at HEAD. Fix: AnthropicLLM.complete and OpenAILLM.complete now call firm.require_unlocked() before the SDK request. That function re-reads firm.yaml on every call. The test makes a client with the lock off, sends one request, then turns the lock on (and separately deletes firm.yaml). After that, complete() and a graph built around the existing client both raise OfflineLockError, and the stand-in SDK records no request. It now passes.

dispositions.finding: src/cma/mcp_server.py:30: the exported MCP server can start under the default lock; only main() was guarded
dispositions.evidence: 24 cases of test_exported_mcp_server_refuses_to_start_under_lock failed at HEAD. Fix: `server` is now a LockedMCPServer subclass. Its run, run_stdio_async, run_sse_async, run_streamable_http_async, sse_app and streamable_http_app all check the lock before the SDK's own start-up. Every tool also checks the lock in _statement() before reading any file, so a call that reaches a tool by another route is refused too (test_mcp_tools_refuse_under_lock). The real embedded server.run() and streamable_http_app() are refused with zero socket audit events.

dispositions.finding: src/cma/graph.py:195: evidence written by resuming a pre-change checkpoint has null egress fields
dispositions.evidence: test_evidence_records_egress_for_a_draft_made_before_the_lock failed at HEAD with two nulls. Fix: graph._egress() falls back for a checkpoint with no lock fields. offline_lock is false, because that version had no lock. destination comes from the stored model name ('fake:' gives offline). recorded says 'at resume; the draft predates the offline lock'. Fresh runs record 'at draft'. The key is additive.

notes:
Attempt 3.

(1) Profile input. The graph and prompt builder have no case-profile input yet; the case store (C3, src/cma/case.py) is another task. So the P5 fixture lays the profile out as the design's case folder, puts its names into the line data, and passes its vat_stagger. A later case-store task that feeds the profile into the graph should keep this test.

(2) Contract change in an MCP tool output (Consumer trace item 8). transactions_for no longer returns untrusted_description and adds description_withheld. R34 requires this. Its only in-repo consumer, tests/test_mcp_paths.py, is updated. External MCP clients that read untrusted_description will no longer get it.

(3) MCP tool calls also refuse under the lock, so tests/test_mcp_paths.py now sets offline_lock: false in a temporary CMA_HOME.

(4) Redraft prompt. The redraft prompt no longer lists which numbers failed. That may make the hosted model's redrafts less targeted; the offline model ignores the feedback either way. R30 allows only tables, period and placeholder, plus this fixed instruction.

(5) urllib3 socket at import. Importing the CLI's dependency chain triggers urllib3's _has_ipv6 probe, which creates and binds a ::1 socket at import time and never connects. It is not a network connection, and it happens before and regardless of the lock.

(6) Not in this task's scope. The reviewer's R34 note says there is no workspace or pack HTML to verify. Escaping there belongs to the C5/C6 tasks; this task neutralises the only CSV writer of payer text (the Monzo importer). synth.py writes only generated text and must stay byte-identical (R47).
